newsitem.title: GERMANY: German roaster unworried by 1997 coffee tightness.
newsitem.headline: German roaster unworried by 1997 coffee tightness.

text.p: German coffee roaster J.J. Darboven on Tuesday dismissed supply worries fuelled by latest news pointing to global supply tightness this year.
"We assume that 1996/97 production will be enough to meet demand," said Guenther Fude, Darboven's head of raw materials purchasing.

He said speculative forces were partly responsible for new two year highs set on New York arabica futures on Monday, which according to traders were triggered by a statement by a U.S. Department of Agriculture offical over the weekend.
A USDA analyst said 1996/97 output could be lower than the 100.9 million bags forecast by the agency last December.
The news enhanced bullishness created by Brazil's dockworker strike threat, signs of lower production in key countries such as Colombia, and globally weak inventories.
Fude said guesswork over the 96/97 and 97/98 balance over the last few weeks had kept the market volatile, sometimes bringing price moves of 10 percent within one trading day.
"Coffee buying has become a lot more difficult," he said.
Darboven says it ranks sixth in the German coffee market and last year sold 25,688 tonnes of roasted coffee (24,000 in 1995) worth 470 million marks (469).
Group chairman Albert Darboven said the company would keep unchanged the typical variety of origins in its blends even in a difficult year, in a bid to maintain quality.
He told Reuters last December the company uses 35-45 percent Colombian.
